ev.q: CDC analyzed 1999–2019 death certificate data, by urban-rural status
From 1999 to 2019, overall age-adjusted COPD mortality rates among women did not change
Differences between men and women in annual age-adjusted COPD mortality rates were smaller in 2019
Age-adjusted rates with 95% CIs were estimated using the 2000 U.S. standard population
Mortality data from the CDC National Vital Statistics System during 1999–2019 were analyzed
Annual percent change (APC) for each trend segment and AAPC from 1999 to 2019 were estimated

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted rates with 95% CIs were estimated using the 2000 U.S. standard population and 10-year age groups.
Annual percent change (APC) for each trend segment and AAPC from 1999 to 2019 were estimated
COPD was identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes J40–J44.
Joinpoint software identifies statistically significant changes in a trend using Monte Carlo permutation
For APCs and for AAPCs within one segment (e.g., no joinpoint), the t-distribution is used.
